title: Pushes to main rebuild every image, not just the changed ones
description:
Each image in this repository has its own push-triggered workflow (`wgcw.yml`, `waml.yml`, `session-complete.yml`, `positron-sagemaker.yml`), and every one of them rebuilds unconditionally on any push to `main`. A change confined to `positron-sagemaker/` still spends runner time rebuilding WGCW, WAML, and Session Complete — the last of which is the largest build in the repo and runs on `ubuntu-latest-8x`.

The product image repositories don't have this problem. They call `posit-dev/images-shared/.github/workflows/bakery-build-native.yml`, which passes `--base-ref ${{ github.event.before }}` to `bakery ci matrix`. Bakery maps the push's changed files onto the image/version matrix and returns an empty matrix when nothing relevant was touched.

These workflows hand-roll their matrix job rather than calling the shared workflow — WGCW needs GCP workload identity federation, and Positron SageMaker needs the SOCI merge job — so they need the same change-awareness applied inline.

Scheduled weekly rebuilds and manual dispatches should continue to build the full matrix.

title: Configure pull-through cache for positron-sagemaker on public ECR
description:
The admin guide for Positron on SageMaker now documents a pull-through cache as an alternative to the manual docker pull/tag/push setup in Step 1. Configuring a pull-through cache in the platform-team account would allow the private `positron-sagemaker` ECR repository to be populated automatically from `public.ecr.aws/posit/positron-sagemaker` on first pull, removing the need for the weekly mirror workflow in platform-infra.

## What this involves

- Create a pull-through cache rule mapping a prefix (e.g. `ecr-public`) to `public.ecr.aws` in the platform-team AWS account
- Add `ecr:BatchImportUpstreamImage` to the SageMaker execution role so Studio Spaces can trigger upstream fetches
- Evaluate whether this replaces or complements the existing scheduled mirror workflow in platform-infra

title: Document a separate Positron space for SageMaker Unified Studio
description:
## Problem

In SageMaker Unified Studio, Positron does not start in the default space
of a project. The app fails with `InternalFailure`.

The cause is the AWS profile. Unified Studio runs a post-startup script on
every launch of the default space. This script writes `~/.aws/config` with
a `[default]` profile that has `credential_source` and no `role_arn`:

```
rm -f /home/sagemaker-user/.aws/config
aws configure set credential_source EcsContainer
```

The AWS CLI accepts this profile. The AWS SDK for Go does not. Our license
client (`license-manager-aws-sagemaker`) uses the Go SDK, so the license
checkout fails:

```
[license-manager] {"errorMessage":"credential type credential_source requires role_arn, profile default","level":"error","msg":"Unable to load SDK config"}
The license manager did not report an activated license. Positron requires a license to run in a hosted environment.
```

If the user has a `~/.aws/config`, `jupyter_server_config.py` does not
override `AWS_CONFIG_FILE`. In Unified Studio this file is always present.
As a result, Positron never uses the baked profile at
`/etc/positron/aws-config`.

## What works today

A user-created space works. Unified Studio does not run the post-startup
script in that space. No `~/.aws/config` exists, so Positron uses the baked
profile and gets a license.

We saw this pattern in 6 launches across 2 Unified Studio domains:

| Space | Post-startup script | Positron |
|---|---|---|
| default space | runs | does not start |
| user-created space | does not run | starts and gets a license |

Note: a user-created space does not have the `DomainExecutionRoleCreds`
profile. Unified Studio features that need this profile do not work there.

## Proposal

Document a separate Positron space. Do not change the default space.

Users keep the default space for Unified Studio work. Users open the
Positron space for Positron work. This split matches the limitation above.

Add these steps to the admin guide and the user guide:

1. Attach the Positron image to the Unified Studio domain.
2. Create a new space in the project.
3. Select the Positron image for this space.
4. Start the space.

Also remove the Studio Lifecycle Config approach from the docs. We tried a
lifecycle config to correct the profile. It never ran. A search of the
`/aws/sagemaker/studio` log group over 3 days returned no output from it.

## Out of scope

An image fix is possible, but it is a separate problem. `positron-server`
runs the binary named by `POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH`. A small wrapper
can pin `AWS_CONFIG_FILE` for that one process, so Positron and the
Unified Studio integration both work. Track this separately.

title: public.ecr.aws/posit/positron-sagemaker tags drifted: :latest/:2026.08.2-4 stale, only :2026.08.2 updated
description:
## Summary

`public.ecr.aws/posit/positron-sagemaker` tags have drifted from each other after the Sept 1 build (PR #74, commit `ff2e2a58`). Only the bare `:2026.08.2` tag was updated to the new build; `:latest`, `:2026.08.2-4`, and both `-ubuntu-24.04` variants are still pinned to the previous day's build (PR #75, commit `cca3f639`).

`ghcr.io/posit-dev/positron-sagemaker` is unaffected — all six alias tags there correctly point at the new build. The drift is isolated to `public.ecr.aws` (confirmed `public.ecr.aws/posit/...` and `public.ecr.aws/m0i8p2s7/...` are the same underlying repo/account, just two registry aliases — not two independent targets).

## Evidence

| Tag | Digest | Commit | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| `:2026.08.2` | `sha256:45c6fd57...` | `ff2e2a58` (Sept 1) | current |
| `:2026.08.2-4` | `sha256:50a243ca...` | `cca3f639` (Aug 31) | stale |
| `:latest` | `sha256:50a243ca...` | `cca3f639` | stale |
| `:2026.08.2-4-ubuntu-24.04` | `sha256:50a243ca...` | `cca3f639` | stale |
| `:2026.08.2-ubuntu-24.04` | `sha256:50a243ca...` | `cca3f639` | stale |
| `:ubuntu-24.04` | `sha256:50a243ca...` | `cca3f639` | stale |

`bakery.yaml` has exactly one `positron-sagemaker` version entry (`2026.08.2-4`), so a single build is meant to fan one image digest out to 12 tag refs (6 ghcr + 6 ECR Public). Only 1 of the 6 ECR Public writes actually stuck.

The Sept 1 run's `Merge/Push positron-sagemaker:2026.08.2-4` job log (run [33537518370](https://github.com/posit-dev/images-specialized/actions/runs/33537518370)) reports success and logs:

```
INFO  Verified ImageTarget(image='positron-sagemaker', version='2026.08.2-4', os='Ubuntu 24.04') ->
      ghcr.io/posit-dev/positron-sagemaker:2026.08.2, ...:2026.08.2-4, ...:2026.08.2-4-ubuntu-24.04,
      ...:2026.08.2-ubuntu-24.04, ...:latest, ...:ubuntu-24.04,
      public.ecr.aws/m0i8p2s7/positron-sagemaker:2026.08.2, ...:2026.08.2-4, ...:2026.08.2-4-ubuntu-24.04,
      ...:2026.08.2-ubuntu-24.04, ...:latest, ...:ubuntu-24.04
```

...i.e. it claims all 12 refs were verified, including the 5 public ECR tags that in fact never moved off the previous build. This is a false positive in `bakery ci publish`'s verify step, specific to `public.ecr.aws` (ghcr's 6 refs are all correctly verified and correct).

## Impact

Anyone pulling `positron-sagemaker:latest` (or `:2026.08.2-4`, or either `-ubuntu-24.04` tag) from public ECR gets a build that is a full day stale relative to `:2026.08.2`, silently.

## Ask

1. Re-run/patch the `merge` job (or manually re-tag) to push `latest`, `2026.08.2-4`, `2026.08.2-4-ubuntu-24.04`, and `2026.08.2-ubuntu-24.04` on `public.ecr.aws/posit/positron-sagemaker` to `sha256:45c6fd57...`, matching `:2026.08.2` and ghcr.
2. File/track upstream in `bakery` (images-shared): `bakery ci publish`'s post-push verification needs to read back *every* pushed tag ref individually on ECR Public rather than trusting a single success signal — it silently missed 5/6 tag writes here while reporting all verified.

title: Add composite action for syncing images to private ECR and SageMaker
description:
Implement a reusable composite action that mirrors a specific tag of `public.ecr.aws/posit/positron-sagemaker` to a private ECR repository and registers a SageMaker ImageVersion.

## Goals

- Mirror public ECR images to private registries for internal use
- Automatically register mirrored images as SageMaker ImageVersions
- Support scheduled runs without manual intervention
- Preserve full OCI artifact trees including SOCI indices

## Implementation details

The action will:
- Accept a tag, source image URI, and target ECR registry as inputs
- Skip ECR copy if the tag already exists in the private registry
- Skip SageMaker registration if the version is already registered
- Poll `describe-image-version` to verify successful registration
- Use ORAS to preserve OCI artifacts and SOCI index during copy
- Provide outputs indicating whether operations were skipped

See the action README for required IAM permissions and usage examples.

## Related

https://github.com/posit-dev/images-specialized/pull/77

title: Pin AWS_CONFIG_FILE for the license client so Positron starts in Unified Studio default spaces
description:
## Problem

Positron does not start in a SageMaker Unified Studio default space. The
app fails with `InternalFailure`. The license checkout is the cause:

```
[license-manager] {"errorMessage":"credential type credential_source requires role_arn, profile default","level":"error","msg":"Unable to load SDK config"}
The license manager did not report an activated license. Positron requires a license to run in a hosted environment.
```

## Cause

Unified Studio runs a post-startup script on every launch of a default
space. This script writes `~/.aws/config` with a `[default]` profile that
has `credential_source` and no `role_arn`:

```
rm -f /home/sagemaker-user/.aws/config
aws configure set credential_source EcsContainer
```

The AWS CLI accepts this profile. The AWS SDK for Go does not.
`license-manager-aws-sagemaker` uses the Go SDK, so it cannot load the
config.

Our image already carries a good profile at `/etc/positron/aws-config`.
`jupyter_server_config.py` (lines 594-611) does not apply it when a user
`~/.aws/config` exists. In Unified Studio this file always exists, so the
baked profile is never used.

## Proposed fix

`positron-server` runs the binary named by `POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH`.
Point that variable at a wrapper. The wrapper pins `AWS_CONFIG_FILE` for
that one process.

### 1. New file: `positron-sagemaker/<version>/license-manager-wrapper`

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# The AWS License Manager client uses the AWS SDK for Go v2. That SDK rejects a
# [default] profile that has credential_source and no role_arn. SageMaker
# Unified Studio writes such a profile to ~/.aws/config on every space launch.
#
# Pin this one process to the baked profile. positron-server, terminals,
# notebooks and the AWS Toolkit keep the AWS config of the user.
#
# AWS_PROFILE is cleared because the baked file defines only [default].
exec env -u AWS_PROFILE AWS_CONFIG_FILE=/etc/positron/aws-config \
  /usr/lib/positron-server/bin/license-manager-aws-sagemaker "$@"
```

### 2. Containerfile

Install the wrapper inside the existing
`if [ -n "${LICENSE_MANAGER_CLIENT_VERSION}" ]` block (lines 318-333). An
image built without the license client then stays the same. The `COPY` must
come before `USER $MAMBA_USER` (line 410).

```
COPY positron-sagemaker/<version>/license-manager-wrapper \
     /usr/lib/positron-server/bin/license-manager-wrapper
RUN chmod 0755 /usr/lib/positron-server/bin/license-manager-wrapper
```

### 3. `jupyter_server_config.py`

Add a wrapper path near line 532. Keep the test for the real client, so the
fallback does not change:

```python
 _LM_CLIENT_PATH = "/usr/lib/positron-server/bin/license-manager-aws-sagemaker"
+_LM_WRAPPER_PATH = "/usr/lib/positron-server/bin/license-manager-wrapper"
 _LM_CLIENT_PRESENT = _os.path.isfile(_LM_CLIENT_PATH) and _os.access(_LM_CLIENT_PATH, _os.X_OK)
+_LM_INVOKE_PATH = (
+    _LM_WRAPPER_PATH
+    if _os.path.isfile(_LM_WRAPPER_PATH) and _os.access(_LM_WRAPPER_PATH, _os.X_OK)
+    else _LM_CLIENT_PATH
+)
```

Then use it in `_lm_vars` near line 541:

```python
-        f"POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH={_LM_CLIENT_PATH}",
+        f"POSITRON_LICENSE_MANAGER_PATH={_LM_INVOKE_PATH}",
```

## Why the fix covers one process only

The stand-down logic at lines 594-611 is correct. Positron must defer to the
AWS config of the user for the IDE. This fix does not change that logic.

The baked profile runs its `credential_process` under
`env -u AWS_CONFIG_FILE -u AWS_PROFILE -u _AWS_CLI_PROFILE_CHAIN`. That
unset already prevents a profile cycle, so the wrapper is safe.

The wrapper also covers lease renewal and the lease return on `SIGTERM`.
Both go through the same entry point.

## Two alternatives we rejected

1. Add `AWS_CONFIG_FILE` to `_lm_vars` only. This is one line, but `_lm_vars`
   goes on the `/usr/bin/env` prefix of the `positron-server` command. Every
   child process inherits it, which includes terminals and R and Python
   sessions.
2. Set `AWS_CONFIG_FILE` in `AppImageConfig`. This needs no image change, but
   it applies to the whole container. `aws configure set` then targets
   `/etc/positron/aws-config`, which is owned by root and is read-only for
   `sagemaker-user`. The three Unified Studio profile writes fail, so
   `DomainExecutionRoleCreds` is never created.

## How to test

Start a default space in a Unified Studio project. The app log must show
both lines:

```
AWS: user config present at /home/sagemaker-user/.aws/config; not overriding AWS_CONFIG_FILE
Positron license acquired from the license manager (days left: ..., users: 50)
```

The first line does not change. That is correct. In the `PostStartup` log
stream, make sure that the script still creates `DomainExecutionRoleCreds`.

## Notes

`AWS_SDK_LOAD_CONFIG=1` is not needed. That variable belongs to v1 of the
AWS SDK for Go. The license client uses v2, which always reads the shared
config.

We saw this failure in 6 launches across 2 Unified Studio domains. A
user-created space is not affected, because Unified Studio does not run the
post-startup script there.
